notes: Works, but it is more invasive (objectFromFileInfo now returns an error, NewObject has convoluted retry logic, zip Open has ad-hoc symlink EOF handling); tests are thorough, including symlink copy and escape.
Identical to C2: production code matches the reference plus docs, with moderate tests that skip range/seek and the unsuffixed NewObject negative checks.

Production code matches the reference exactly and adds a useful docs section; tests cover basic zip listing/reading, squashfs via mksquashfs and the escape case, but there are no range/seek or NewObject-negative checks.

Clean implementation that supports both root forms and clamps zip symlink offsets; tests are thorough and use a binary squashfs fixture instead of an external tool, though it refactors the existing writeZip helper and fails listing if Readlink is unavailable.
Production code matches the reference minimally and correctly, with docs and the best tests of the reference-equivalent patches (range/seek, NewObject negatives, regular .rclonelink, escape).

Large two-pass readZip rewrite handles symlink/regular name collisions, but a root given as the listed name (link.txt.rclonelink) is not recognised in either backend, breaking listing/lookup agreement; the test also uses os.Chdir.

Correct for both backends and also accepts a single-file root given with or without the suffix, though the new zip withinRoot helper and the two-pass squashfs lookup add complexity; tests cover listing, NewObject agreement, range/seek, regular .rclonelink names, single root, copy and escape.
